entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Registered through the ROUTES list in app.py, which imports the account module.

entry_points.name: purge_closed_accounts
entry_points.note: Celery task run on the beat schedule declared in config.py.

stores.name: users

fields.name: signup_ip
fields.note: Holds the IP address the account was created from.

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: The application's own marker for a closed account; the purge job selects rows on it.

erasure.note: close_account only writes deleted_at; the row is removed by session.delete in purge_closed_accounts once deleted_at is older than RETENTION_DAYS, and that task is on the Celery beat schedule in config.py.

stores.note: Single table defined in models.py and created from the declarative base in db.py.

stores.name: uploads/avatars

fields.name: avatar_key
fields.note: The object key is built from the user id.

fields.name: original_filename
fields.note: The name of the file as the uploader supplied it, stored as S3 object metadata.

erasure.note: cleanup_user_files is the only call that deletes the object and nothing in the repository calls it; neither close_account nor the purge task touches object storage, although the close_account docstring says uploaded files are removed.

stores.note: Avatar images written by set_avatar into the bucket named by the BUCKET constant.

stores.name: stripe

fields.name: name
fields.note: The user's full_name is sent as the customer name.

erasure.note: The repository creates a Stripe customer at signup and contains no call that deletes or redacts it.

stores.note: Stripe customer created from the signup route in api/profile.py.

stores.name: nightly_backup

fields.name: email
fields.note: Named in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row into the dump file.

fields.name: full_name
fields.note: Named in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each User row into the dump file.

erasure.note: dump_database writes every User row to a JSON file; BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS is declared in the same module and no code in the repository reads it or removes the file.

stores.note: JSON dump of the users table written to the path built from BACKUP_NAME.

retention.criteria: rows whose deleted_at is older than the cutoff are deleted by the purge task
